rv.q: This National Tour is tighter and cleans up some of the grittier sensibilities while employing Broadway level talent.
This beautiful production comes with all the old-fashioned charm which had the audience cheering at that final curtain.
This touring production hits all the right notes.

This production glows with nostalgia swirling around ice cream socials, patriotic pageants, and a lovable con man redeemed by the rubes he wants to con, fashioned with old-fashioned Broadway know-how, and those Willson ballads and marches that we all know by heart.

Despite this musical often verging on off-putting levels of chipper cheeriness, the beloved jaunty tunes, elaborate set design/projections, and mesmerizing choreography elevated this touring production of The Music Man.
Andrews plays him too earnestly, and it makes the Act II reveal of his true intentions feel jarring and cruel.

cn.t: This touring production of Meredith Willson's classic musical delights with energetic song-and-dance numbers and old-fashioned Americana charm, proving the beloved show's warmth and spectacle still resonate nearly 70 years after its Broadway debut.
